title: Καρκῖνος καὶ μήτηρ
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 151. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Μὴ λοξὰ περιπατεῖν καρκίνῳ μήτηρ ⟨ἔλεγε⟩ μηδὲ τῇ ὑγρᾷ πέτρᾳ τὰς πλευρὰς προστρίβειν.
sentences.tr: Mē loxa peripatein karkinōi mētēr ⟨elege⟩ mēde tēi hygrāi petrāi tas pleuras prostribein.
sentences.l: Not to walk crooked the mother ⟨was telling⟩ the crab, nor to rub his sides against the wet rock.
sentences.i: The mother kept telling the crab not to walk sideways, nor to scrape his sides against the wet rock.
sentences.n: ⟨ἔλεγε⟩ stands in angle brackets because it is Chambry's own supplement: the text as transmitted has no governing verb, and he adds one. It is imperfect — the telling was repeated. λοξά is a neuter plural adjective doing an adverb's work, "aslant". The infinitives carry the content of the command, with μή and μηδέ as the negatives commands take.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· « Μῆτερ, σύ, ἡ διδάσκουσα, ὀρθὰ βάδιζε καὶ βλέπων σε ζηλώσω. »
sentences.tr: Ho de eipen· « Mēter, sy, hē didaskousa, ortha badize kai blepōn se zēlōsō. »
sentences.l: And he said: « Mother, you, the one who teaches, walk straight, and seeing you I shall emulate you. »
sentences.i: And he said: « Mother, you who do the teaching — walk straight yourself, and when I see you I shall follow your example. »
sentences.n: ἡ διδάσκουσα is a participle with the article set in apposition to σύ: "you, the one who does the teaching". ὀρθά answers the λοξά of the first line, again a neuter plural used as an adverb. ζηλόω is to look on someone with emulation and copy him; the crab does not deny the charge, but makes his mother's own walk the condition of mending his.

sentences.t: Ὅτι τοὺς μεμψιμοίρους πρέπον ἐστὶν ὀρθὰ βιοῦν καὶ βαδίζειν, καὶ τότε ὅμοια διδάσκειν.
sentences.tr: Hoti tous mempsimoirous prepon estin ortha bioun kai badizein, kai tote homoia didaskein.
sentences.l: That it is fitting for those who find fault to live and to walk straight, and only then to teach the like.
sentences.i: The story shows that it is fitting for those who find fault to live and walk straight themselves, and only then to teach others the same.
sentences.n: A moral in the bare Ὅτι form: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek, which begins simply "That…", and is supplied in the idiomatic line. πρέπον ἐστίν is an impersonal built on the neuter participle and takes the accusative with the infinitive. μεμψίμοιρος is literally one who blames his allotted portion, a grumbler; here it stands for those who find fault with others. ὅμοια, neuter plural, is "the like things".
